content.title: About
content.content: Gelatin shots are small, single‑serve alcoholic drinks presented as jelly. They are typically made from food‑grade gelatin, fruit juice, sugar and a spirit (vodka, rum, tequila, etc.). The shot melts in the mouth, leaving a sweet aftertaste and a mild buzz.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gelatin shots gained popularity in the United States in the early 2000s as a novel way to serve cocktails.
The gelatin used is derived from animal collagen found in bones and skin.
Shots are often colored brightly, making them eye‑catching at parties.
A typical shot contains 5–15 % alcohol by volume, but the strength can vary widely.
Some countries restrict the sale of alcoholic gelatin shots because of the risk of rapid consumption.

items.title: Fast absorption
items.content: The gelatin matrix speeds up alcohol absorption, which may reduce the waiting time for its effects.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Added sugar provides a quick boost of glucose.

items.title: Fruit‑derived vitamins
items.content: When natural juices are used, the shot can supply vitamin C and other antioxidants.

items.title: Rapid intoxication
items.content: Because alcohol is absorbed quickly, blood‑alcohol levels can rise sharply.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The sugar load may be unsuitable for people with diabetes or weight concerns.

items.title: Gelatin allergy
items.content: Gelatin can trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to animal proteins.

items.title: Not for children or pregnant women
items.content: Alcoholic shots are prohibited for minors, pregnant, and nursing women.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Take the shot with a spoon or place it in the mouth and let it fully dissolve. Serve chilled, sometimes garnished with berries or edible glitter.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep prepared shots in the refrigerator at 2–4 °C in an airtight container for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze them in individual molds.
